source.display_title: 06/09/2026 - Jorge Alfonso x Ben Byrne  — Closed

setter.evidence: No setter suffix in the title and no setter named. The call was originally booked to a different closer and handed over at short notice: 'I was expecting like an Andrew, I think' answered with 'Yeah, Andrew, I think, I'm not sure something happened with his schedule, so he asked me to take the call.'

prospect.name: Jorge Alfonso
prospect.location: Spain (Belgian mobile number, +32); describes himself as 'Cuban, Mexican, Belgian'
prospect.occupation: Consultant and owner of his own business in talent advisory and contingent workforce management. Sedentary — 'I'm mostly behind a computer.' Travels enough to derail training; recently spent half a month away.
prospect.family_status: Two young children; drives them to school around 08:45. Has moved countries twice in recent years.
prospect.training_background: Former Division 1 basketball player and semi-professional athlete; also played American football. Training in proper gyms since age 16 and using kettlebells for decades — 'it's not like I went to school for kettlebells, but... I'm also not doing a poor hinge when I use them.' Nothing consistent for three to four years. Last good stretch was 2022, playing padel two to four hours a day and losing 15-20 kg. Started at a gym about six weeks ago and stopped when work travel intervened. Plays padel obsessively in season but it is currently too hot. Already owns kettlebells — 'they're literally 10 feet away from me now.' Tried the Knees Over Toes programme, which did not help.
prospect.medical: Catastrophic knee injury at 19 — a torn ACL plus three of the four ligaments in a single injury, which he calls an anomaly. Was advised to retire at around 24-25 and carried on playing basketball and American football until 27-28, compounding the damage: 'I did a lot of damage when I just couldn't go anymore because the pain was just too high to tolerate.' Now has severe osteoarthritis in the knee, bone-on-bone, with recurring bone spurs, meniscus tweaks and ligament pain — 'it is quite painful' and 'it's not something that you can just take a painkiller and go back out there.' Recovery from any lower-body tweak takes a very long time. No current clinician, imaging or clearance was mentioned, and none was asked about.

signals: Lost a career and a body to injury and has been sliding since — 'I was politely asked to retire' and 'since then, it's all been just like an uphill ballooning stage'
Wants a former capability back rather than a new one, and is explicit that aesthetics are not the point — 'I just want to be able to play with my kids whenever I want to, and not have a gut'
Carries the regret plainly, including about ignoring medical advice — 'I didn't really listen, because you can't tell an athlete to retire, that's impossible'

Secondary read is the_medically_constrained: high intent and literally zero price resistance ('All right. That's fine.'), blocked by an injury the programme may not be able to work around. Rejected as primary only because nothing blocked him — he bought.
Not skeptical_bargain_hunter despite comparing creators: the comparison was on programme sustainability, never on price

goals.text: Be consistent — the stated primary goal, ahead of any outcome: 'my goal is to stay consistent, and then the result will materialize'
Lose the gut — 'I just found myself with time and a big belly that I did not want to have anymore'
Be able to play with his kids whenever he wants to
Be healthy and mobile rather than lean — 'I don't aim to look like Trevor. I don't want my veins popping out'
Train without further damaging the knee
Find something he will actually return to — 'does the program actually make me want to come back? Do I find myself being captivated?'
Bring calorie intake in line with a sedentary life — 'I do eat as if I was a 20-some-year-old athlete, which I'm not'

pains.text: No external accountability, which he names as the whole problem — 'If I'm the one that's holding myself accountable, that's probably not going to happen'
Bone-on-bone knee osteoarthritis with bone spurs and recurring pain from a four-ligament rupture
Three to four years without consistent training
Every prior programme disconnected after delivery — 'they send you either PDF or they give you a link to an app and then they sort of disconnect from you'
Injuries repeatedly kill his momentum — 'Usually an injury gets in the way... I'm not in a position where I can recover quickly'
Eating at athlete volume on a sedentary lifestyle — 'my calorie consumption is through the roof'
Work travel breaks any routine — started at a gym six weeks ago and 'work got in the way and I spent half a month traveling so I couldn't follow through'
Self-described lack of discipline — 'You can put that together with my own lack of discipline'
Two young children and a business leave no time for himself — 'you don't really get a lot of time for yourself'
Overwhelmed by kettlebell content — 'I get 700 other content creators' and programmes with 'these crazy complexes and 700 exercises every time'

objections.raw_quote: I would love to tell you I'm 100% committed, but reality is I've been there before and it hasn't worked out. So I'm also not going to lie to you. I want to.
objections.rep_response: Answered with a certainty claim about the programme rather than addressing the doubt about himself: 'in many ways, it's like other programs. As long as you're doing it and you're following the process and you're eating right, I mean, it's pretty hard for it not to work.' Then moved directly to price. No return to the consequence frame, which is what the script prescribes when hesitation surfaces.

objections.raw_quote: Of course, I don't know how the program actually works. With any situation like this, you have rights and responsibilities, so I have no clue what I'm entitled to, nor do I know what my responsibilities are. So that would be the main question.
objections.rep_response: Answered with the three-step process and the delivery mechanics — app, form review, check-ins, group sessions — and never addressed terms, entitlements, cancellation or obligations at any point in the call.

evidence: Unambiguous verbal agreement to proceed: 'You send me an invoice, I pay it' and 'So I make the payment, I get a link, email, whatever the case might be, login, details, and then the onboarding happens when it happens. Yeah? Did I get that correctly?'
Payment link sent and opened live: 'I'll drop a link here in the chat' and 'I have the link open.'
Onboarding call with Trevor booked on the call for Tuesday 1:15pm Eastern, with email and Belgian mobile number captured.
Zero price resistance — the $6,000 six-month price was answered with 'All right. That's fine.'

Counter-evidence, material: no funds were collected. Payment is a cross-border bank transfer taking two to three business days — 'because I'm in Europe, it won't be an instant money transfer' — with no card taken as a fallback and no follow-up mechanism beyond 'just shoot me a message whenever it goes through.'

Counter-evidence: the prospect explicitly declined to claim commitment fifteen minutes before agreeing — 'I would love to tell you I'm 100% committed, but reality is I've been there before and it hasn't worked out.'
Counter-evidence: no agreement was signed on the call; the rep described it as arriving only after payment processes.
outcome.cash_collection_basis: pending_bank_transfer — $6,000 six-month contract agreed verbally with the link opened, but no funds received on the call; settlement dependent on a two-to-three-day cross-border transfer from Spain. Recorded as closed under the verbal-agreement-plus-link-sent rule, not on cash.
outcome.next_step: Prospect to initiate a bank transfer for $6,000; on receipt he gets the agreement to sign, the onboarding email, app and community access and the onboarding form. Trevor onboarding call already booked for Tuesday 1:15pm Eastern. Rep to text him on WhatsApp so contact exists outside email.

notable.note: A close recorded on a verbal agreement with no money taken and settlement dependent on a multi-day international transfer, on a prospect who said plainly he could not honestly claim he was committed. The bigger issue is clinical: bone-on-bone knee osteoarthritis with recurring bone spurs, following a four-ligament rupture and a medical recommendation to retire that he ignored for several years — and nobody asked whether any clinician had cleared him for loaded kettlebell training. He also asked directly what he was entitled to and what his responsibilities were, and was never told. The call was handed over from Andrew Musial to Ben Byrne at short notice, so the deal sits in the wrong rep folder for attribution purposes. Minor conduct note: the rep opened by joking about the absent colleague's nationality — 'He's Polish anyway, so probably going to be grumpy.'

quality.notes: Heavily inverted, including on identity-defining lines. 'I'm in Spain' at 00:00:34 and 'I'm Cuban, but' at 00:00:38 are both labelled to the rep but are the prospect — the rep confirms much later that he is in Canada, 'an hour ahead of Eastern'. 'He's a hot dude' about Trevor at 00:14:31 is the prospect. 'I'm black, so I expect to have results in six months' at 00:31:03 is labelled to the rep and is plainly the prospect. The consulting-work exchange at 00:32:43 has the question and answer under the wrong names. Roles resolved from content throughout. Height and weight were never asked or stated at any point despite weight loss being a stated goal, so both are null; the only weight datum in the call is a 15-20 kg loss during 2022.
